units.source: Multicolumn layout
units.context: Multicolumn layout

units.source: A multicolumn layout arranges content in two to four columns, side by side. A column can hold any kind of content, including tables, images and another multicolumn layout.
units.context: Multicolumn layout

units.source: Inserting a layout__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Inserting a layout

units.source: In the formatting bar, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Insert__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__ __TRILIUM_PH_3__Columns__TRILIUM_PH_4__ to insert a layout with two columns. Its submenu offers __TRILIUM_PH_5__2 columns__TRILIUM_PH_6__, __TRILIUM_PH_7__3 columns__TRILIUM_PH_8__ and __TRILIUM_PH_9__4 columns__TRILIUM_PH_10__.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Inserting a layout

units.source: Alternatively, type __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and choose __TRILIUM_PH_1__2 columns layout__TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__3 columns layout__TRILIUM_PH_4__ or __TRILIUM_PH_5__4 columns layout__TRILIUM_PH_6__, as described in __TRILIUM_PH_7__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_8__.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Inserting a layout

units.source: The columns of a new layout have equal widths. If text is selected when the layout is inserted, the selection moves into the first column.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Inserting a layout

units.source: Adding columns__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Changing the columns > Adding columns

units.source: While the cursor is in a column, you can use these key combinations:
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Changing the columns > Adding columns

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__: Add a column after the current one.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Changing the columns > Adding columns

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_3__ + __TRILIUM_PH_4__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_5__: Add a column before the current one.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Changing the columns > Adding columns

units.source: The new column is empty and the cursor moves into it. All the columns then have equal widths. A layout has at most four columns, so the keys do nothing in a layout that already has four.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Changing the columns > Adding columns

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__ keeps its usual function on a link, in a to-do item and in the title of a collapsible block, and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_5__ + __TRILIUM_PH_6__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_7__ + __TRILIUM_PH_8__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_9__ in a to-do item.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Changing the columns > Adding columns

units.source: Reordering columns__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Changing the columns > Reordering columns

units.source: While the cursor is anywhere inside a column, you can use these key combinations:
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Changing the columns > Reordering columns

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_3__ + __TRILIUM_PH_4__Right__TRILIUM_PH_5__: Move the column to the right.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Changing the columns > Reordering columns

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_3__ + __TRILIUM_PH_4__Left__TRILIUM_PH_5__: Move the column to the left.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Changing the columns > Reordering columns

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_3__ + __TRILIUM_PH_4__Home__TRILIUM_PH_5__: Make it the first column.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Changing the columns > Reordering columns

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_3__ + __TRILIUM_PH_4__End__TRILIUM_PH_5__: Make it the last column.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Changing the columns > Reordering columns

units.source: In a layout with two columns of different widths, the column keeps its width.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Changing the columns > Reordering columns

units.source: Moving content between columns__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Moving content between columns

units.source: To move content to another column, select it, and then use these key combinations:
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Moving content between columns

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Right__TRILIUM_PH_3__: Move to the column on the right.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Moving content between columns

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Left__TRILIUM_PH_3__: Move to the column on the left.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Moving content between columns

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_3__ + __TRILIUM_PH_4__End__TRILIUM_PH_5__: Move to the last column.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Moving content between columns

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_3__ + __TRILIUM_PH_4__Home__TRILIUM_PH_5__: Move to the first column.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Moving content between columns

units.source: Paragraphs, list items, tables and other blocks move whole, even when only part of them is selected. Content moved to a column on the left goes to the end of that column, and content moved to a column on the right goes to its start, so it keeps its place in the reading order.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Moving content between columns

units.source: Without a selection, these keys keep their usual function: moving the cursor by word, or selecting up to the start or end of the column.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Moving content between columns

units.source: When a layout and __TRILIUM_PH_0__Content tabs__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are nested in one another, the key combinations act on the one closest to the cursor.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Moving content between columns

units.source: Removing a layout__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Removing a layout

units.source: To remove the layout but keep its content, click the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Remove layout__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button in the layout's toolbar. The content of the columns is placed one after another where the layout was, and empty columns are left out.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Removing a layout

units.source: To delete the layout together with its content, click the handle at its top-left corner to select it, then press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Delete__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Removing a layout

units.source: Narrow screens__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Narrow screens

units.source: When a layout has too little room for its columns (narrower than about 500 pixels, such as on a phone), the columns are stacked one below the other. While editing, alternating background colors tell the columns apart. This applies to each layout on its own, so a layout inside a narrow column is stacked while the outer one stays side by side.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Narrow screens

units.source: Printing and exporting__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Printing and exporting

units.source: When printing or __TRILIUM_PH_0__exporting to PDF__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the columns are printed side by side.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Printing and exporting

units.source: Markdown has no columns, so Markdown export keeps the layout and each column as HTML __TRILIUM_PH_0__ tags, with the content of each column written as Markdown between them. Importing the file back restores the layout. Markdown viewers that don't support HTML show the content of the columns one after another.
units.context: Multicolumn layout > Printing and exporting
